---

# The year in review

January opened with a deploy that took forty minutes and a staging environment nobody trusted enough to test against. We spent most of Q1 on both. Deploys are down to six minutes, and staging now runs the same data shape as production, which is why the December freeze was the first one in three years where nobody got paged at 2am.

The billing extraction took longer than we said it would. We estimated two quarters and it ran three and a half. The reason is worth writing down. The old module had four undocumented callers, and we only found them by turning it off in staging and waiting for something to break. The service inventory work that started in August exists so we never have to find callers that way again.

The numbers, roughly. We shipped 214 changes to customers, closed 61 percent of the incident backlog, and went from nine engineers to fourteen. Everyone who joined in the spring was shipping in their first month, which says more about the onboarding rewrite than about our hiring luck.

The search rewrite is the one that did not go well. It has been half-finished since May. Nobody in particular is at fault, and that is the problem with it. It needs a single owner in January, and I would rather that owner volunteered than got assigned.

Thanks for a good year. Go take the holidays properly, and we will pick it up in the new year.
